stdout.text:
{"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse", "permissionDecision": "allow", "additionalContext": "Plan for src/lifelike/rule.py (ART-RULE), from .aes/target.yaml:
Part of OUT-001: They name a pattern and a Life-like rule written in B/S
  notation (for example B3/S23) and watch the pattern evolve generation by
  generation as ASCII art in their terminal, and every known pattern behaves
  exactly as the mathematics of that rule says it must.
BEH-RULE: A rule written in B/S notation (B, then the live-neighbour counts
  that bring a dead cell to life, a slash, S, then the counts that keep a
  live cell alive; each count one digit 0 to 8) is read into its birth and
  survival sets. A named rule stands for its notation: `life` is B3/S23 and
  `highlife` is B36/S23. Any other text is rejected with ValueError naming
  that text.
SC-RULE: B3/S23 and `life` read as birth {3} and survival {2, 3}; B36/S23
  and `highlife` read as birth {3, 6} and survival {2, 3}; malformed text is
  rejected.
  Disproved if: A rule reads into the wrong sets, `highlife` is not B36/S23,
  or text such as `B9/S23`, `3/23` or an empty string is accepted.
Proven by: VS-RULE (tests/test_rule.py)
Declares (typed signatures, from the plan):
  Rule
  parse_rule(text: str) -> Rule"}}
